propositions: A class may reference a model that is intermittently unreachable (local endpoint down, provider throttled), and today a single failure fails the gate with no fallback option.
Fallback entries are inline model configs (same shape as a slot) with endpoint honored, not named preset references, so operators need not learn rebar vocabulary.

The fallback_on predicate must be narrowed to errors where switching providers helps (RETRY_NOW, WAIT_AND_RETRY, CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL) rather than all exceptions, because a 429 rate-limit or CONNECT_ERROR can be resolved by failover, but a 401 credential or 400 context-length error cannot.

Capabilities, cache settings, and tool-capability guards are computed from the resolved candidate list (primary plus all fallbacks) as a conservative intersection before the FallbackModel wrapper is built, so a capability holds only if every candidate has it.

The model provenance must record both the ordered candidates and the ran_model read from the ModelResponse.model_name, never the FallbackModel.model_name synthetic string, so a verdict produced by a fallback does not attest the wrong model.

The FallbackModel must be used as an async context manager so pydantic-ai's own sub-provider clients are entered and closed, while rebar-created retrying transports remain registered on ProviderSession._closeables and are closed exactly once.
